journey.step1Body: Ein kurzes Gespräch über Ihr Ziel, Ihre Kunden und Ihren Termin. Ohne Fachjargon und ohne Druck.

timeline.a: Eine übersichtliche Website dauert in der Regel zwei bis vier Wochen. Eine maßgeschneiderte Plattform oder ein E-Commerce-Shop benötigt sechs bis zwölf Wochen.

stack.a: Individuelle Projekte entwickeln wir mit React und Next.js, unterstützt von Supabase für Datenbank und Authentifizierung. Bei passenden Anforderungen setzen wir auch auf WordPress und Wix.

ownership.a: Ja, zu 100%. Sie erhalten das uneingeschränkte Eigentum am Quellcode, an den Designs und allen Accounts samt Videoanleitung.

support.a: Jedes Projekt beinhaltet 30 Tage kostenfreie Betreuung nach dem Launch. Danach können Sie die Pflege selbst übernehmen oder ein monatliches Wartungspaket buchen.

payments.a: Projekte werden in eine Anzahlung und Meilensteinzahlungen aufgeteilt. Zahlung per Kreditkarte, Überweisung oder lokalen Zahlungsmethoden in Ihrer Währung.

start.a: Senden Sie uns eine Nachricht über das Kontaktformular oder buchen Sie ein kurzes Gespräch. Wir antworten innerhalb von zwei Werktagen mit einem klaren Fahrplan und Festpreis.

sections.heading: Who we are
sections.body: Virtue & Co. Webworks is a web design and development studio working with clients worldwide. We are the data controller for information collected through this website.

sections.heading: What we collect
sections.body: When you submit the contact form we collect your name, email address and the project details you choose to share, including an optional phone number, company name, budget band and timeline. When you subscribe to the newsletter we collect only your email address. When you make a payment we collect the billing details required to process it.

sections.heading: How we use it
sections.body: We use your information to answer your enquiry, prepare a proposal, deliver work you have engaged us for, and send the newsletter you asked for. We do not sell personal information, and we do not use it for advertising.

sections.heading: Cookies and local storage
sections.body: We store your language and colour-theme preferences in your browser so the site behaves consistently on return visits. We may use privacy-respecting, anonymous analytics to understand which pages are useful. No advertising trackers are used.

sections.heading: Payments
sections.body: Card payments are processed securely by certified payment processors. Card numbers never reach our servers; we store only a transaction reference, the amount, the currency and the status so that invoices can be reconciled.

sections.heading: Third parties
sections.body: We use a small number of processors to run the site and communicate with you, including Supabase (database and authentication), Vercel (hosting), and Resend (transactional email). Each processes data only as needed to provide that service.

sections.heading: Retention
sections.body: Enquiries are kept for up to three years so we can pick a conversation back up. Newsletter subscriptions are kept until you unsubscribe. Payment records are kept as long as tax and accounting rules require.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You can ask us for a copy of the information we hold about you, ask us to correct or delete it, or withdraw consent for the newsletter at any time by replying to any email we send.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: Write to virtueco.dev@gmail.com for any privacy request and we will respond within two business days.

terms.title: Allgemeine Geschäftsbedingungen
terms.metaDescription: Vertragsbedingungen, Urheberrechte, Garantien und Meilensteine bei Virtue & Co. Webworks.
terms.intro: Diese Bedingungen regeln alle Web-Engineering- und Designdienstleistungen unseres Studios transparent und fair.

sections.heading: Agreement
sections.body: An engagement begins when you accept a written proposal and pay the deposit it specifies. The proposal sets out the scope, the price, the timeline and the deliverables for your project.

sections.heading: Quotes and pricing
sections.body: Quotes are valid for 30 days and are fixed for the scope described. Prices are shown in US Dollars unless your proposal states otherwise. The currency you are invoiced in is agreed in the proposal and is not adjusted for exchange-rate movement during the project.

sections.heading: Payment terms
sections.body: Projects are split into a deposit and milestone payments, typically 50% to begin and the balance on delivery. Retainers are invoiced monthly in advance. Work may be paused if an invoice is overdue by more than 14 days.

sections.heading: Client responsibilities
sections.body: You agree to provide content, brand assets, access and timely feedback. Delays in supplying these shift the delivery date by at least the length of the delay.

sections.heading: Revisions and scope changes
sections.body: Each phase includes two rounds of revisions. Anything beyond the agreed scope is quoted separately and only starts once you approve that quote in writing.

sections.heading: Intellectual property
sections.body: On final payment you own the deliverables, including the source code, design files and content we produced for you. We retain the right to showcase the work in our portfolio unless we agree otherwise in writing.

sections.heading: Warranty and support
sections.body: We fix defects in what we delivered, free of charge, for 30 days after launch. Ongoing changes, new features and third-party maintenance are covered by a support retainer.

sections.heading: Liability
sections.body: Our total liability for any engagement is limited to the fees you paid for it. We are not liable for indirect or consequential losses, including lost profit or lost data.

sections.heading: Termination
sections.body: Either party may end an engagement with 14 days written notice. Work completed up to that point is invoiced and payable, and completed deliverables are handed over on settlement.

sections.heading: Governing law
sections.body: These terms are governed by the laws named in your proposal, and the courts sitting in that jurisdiction have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute. Where a proposal does not name a jurisdiction, the laws and courts of the studio's place of business apply.
